machine: GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB on a whole ASPIRE 2A node; CPU: AMD EPYC 7713 on a whole ASPIRE 2A node
dtype: float32 on GPU and CPU-parallel, float64 in the serial C++ kernel
protocol: experiments/bench_unified_timing.py: uniform runoff 2 mm/day, steady state of that forcing shared by all configurations, 10 warm-up steps then the mean over 600 routing time steps (one month at 4,320 s), 4 Newton steps; SURGE compiled with torch.compile, three repeats with the median; CPU runs once each on a node used by no other job; CPU-parallel on 24 threads; serial = CWatM t5 C++ kernel on one core
source: one set of timing runs on ASPIRE 2A, 2026-11-23/24: all four configurations, and the runs with and without the dams, from the same jobs
note: Values are wall-clock in milliseconds per routing time step; a simulated day is 20 steps. SURGE and CPU-parallel are timed at the iteration count each river network needs to match the serial solution (field k); CPU-serial and GPU-ordered do not iterate.
